lee: quick heads-up — during the surge sim at ~14:03 UTC we saw p99 spike ~3x for ~120s after the autoscaler added 2 nodes. observed kernel fallback events and a sharp KV miss-rate increase. attaching a tiny profile/log snippet. :eyes:

maria: can you paste the logs and the kernel variants that were active? was batching changing too?

lee: pasted below. microbatch target collapsed to 1 for many streams when SLO tightened, and prober seemed to pick a different kernel late.

lee: ```
[14:03:12] req=0 microbatch=1 kernel=v1 fastpath=true kv_hit=false
[14:03:12] prober: sampled kernel=v2 for seq=1024 (score delta +12)
[14:03:13] autoscaler: request->scaleup triggered (provisioning 2 nodes)
[14:03:14] host-23: kv-miss-rate=0.68
[14:03:14] runtime: kernel fallback v2->v0 (hopback) cost=118ms p99=920ms
[14:05:15] recovery: kv-hit stabilized, p99 returns to baseline
```

oliver: that hopback cost + cold KV on new hosts seems likely. did we see any queueing between microbatch boundaries? could be that microbatch=1 amplifies per-request kernel switch penalties.

lee: queue-length stayed low (tail not from queuing). hypothesize: (1) new nodes come up cold -> KV misses; (2) prober/selector switches kernel variant across hosts creating hop penalty for migrating streams; (3) microbatch reduction to 1 removes amortization of kernel switch cost.

anu: makes sense. two quick mitigations to try: eager KV-prefetch on scaleup + delay kernel switch until prober sample_count >= threshold. both should reduce transient p99.

devon: i ran a small local sim: prewarm-kv on join + probe-threshold=50 => p99 improved ~30% on surge. quick commands i used:```
# simulate scaleup warmup (local harness)
python tools/sim_scale.py --qps 1000 --scale-to 4 --warmup-kv --probe-threshold 50 
# collect traces
python infra/collect_traces.py --trace-only kernel_switch,kv_fetch --out out.json
```

lee: good start. let's run a proper A/B: A=current rollout, B=prewarm+probe-threshold=50 + microbatch_min=4 for 10m surge. add kernel-switch time tracing. @maria @anu any objections?

maria: no objections. i'll add dashboard panels: "kernel-switch latency", "kv-miss-rate by host", and "prober-sample-count". will also hook the flamegraph upload to the experiment ticket.

sre-bot: experiment ticket created: INF-1423 assigned to @maria, @lee, expected duration 2h. :white_check_mark:

oliver: :thumbsup: i'll help with trace correlation and generate flamegraphs from out.json once the run finishes.

lee: thanks all — i'll schedule the 30m 10x-surge run for tomorrow 14:00 UTC and post results here. trying to keep the change small (no structural runtime change yet) so we can validate impact purely from warmup + probe tuning. :rocket!
